problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(0,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-3<X<3)=0.8472,$ use the table to find $\sigma ,$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.3\,$ | $\,0.9066\,$ | $\,0.9082\,$ | $\,0.9099\,$ |
| $\,1.4\,$ | $\,0.9222\,$ | $\,0.9236\,$ | $\,0.9251\,$ |
| $\,1.5\,$ | $\,0.9357\,$ | $\,0.9370\,$ | $\,0.9382\,$ |

$\sigma ≈$

activity_context.topic_title: Mean and Variance of the Normal Distribution

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we express the given probability as

$$
P(|X|<9)=P(-9<X<9).
$$

Then, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-9<X<9) & =0.5468 \\ 2P(0<X<9) & =0.5468 \\ P(0<X<9) & =0.2374 \\ P(X<9)-P(X<0) & =0.2734 \\ P(X<9)-0.5 & =0.2734 \\ P(X<9) & =0.7734 \\ P(X\le 9) & =0.7734\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 9) & =0.7734 \\ P(Z\le \frac{9-0}{\sigma }) & =0.7734 \\ Φ(\frac{9}{\sigma }) & =0.7734 \\ \frac{9}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.7734)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.75)=0.7734\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.7734)=0.75.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{\sigma } & =0.75 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{9}{0.75} \\ \sigma  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =(12)^{2}=144.\end{aligned}
$$
